    StartersMiles's birthday caramel popcorn ballsPopcorn and marshmallow caramel balls rolled in rainbow sprinklesHow to make it100g popcorn kernels2 tbsp vegetable oil60g butter200g marshmallows80g brown sugar50g rainbow sprinklesPop the kernels in the oil in a covered pot and tip into a big bowl, discarding unpopped kernels.Melt the butter, marshmallows and brown sugar over low heat, stirring until smooth, with a pinch of salt.Pour over the popcorn and stir quickly to coat. Cool briefly.With buttered hands squeeze into balls and roll in the sprinkles.Set on baking paper.Bowling night cheesy gravy chipsChicken salted chips with melted cheddar and beef gravyHow to make it1kg frozen chips1 tsp chicken salt30g butter2 tbsp plain flour400ml beef stock1 tsp Worcestershire sauce150g cheddar, grated1 small bunch chives, choppedBake the chips at 220°C, turning once, then toss with chicken salt.Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock and Worcestershire. Simmer until thick and glossy.Pile the chips on a platter, scatter with cheddar and pour over the hot gravy.Finish with chives.Cheese and bacon hash brownsKeep the engine running, the car backfires.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsBuck's big breakfast for dinnerEggs, sausages, bacon, hash browns and baked beans with toastHow to make it8 frozen hash browns8 pork sausages8 rashers of bacon420g tin baked beans8 eggs60ml full cream milk60g butter8 slices of white bread1 bottle tomato sauceBake the hash browns at 220°C until crisp.Fry the sausages over medium heat, turning.Fry the bacon until crisp.Warm the baked beans.Whisk the eggs with the milk and salt and cook in some of the butter over low heat, stirring gently, until just set.Toast and butter the bread. Pile everything onto big plates with tomato sauce.Buck's family-size beef lasagneBuck cooks for an army, then makes the kids eat it all weekHow to make it600g beef mince1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, crushed700g tomato passata250g dried lasagne sheets40g butter40g plain flour500ml milk200g mozzarella, grated1 cos lettuce2 tomatoes2 tbsp olive oilBrown the mince in the oil, add the onion and garlic, then the passata, and simmer.Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then whisk in the milk until thick.Heat the oven to 180°C. Layer the ragù, pasta and white sauce in a dish, finishing with sauce and mozzarella.Bake until golden and bubbling, then rest. Serve with the lettuce and tomato.SweetsUncle Buck's giant buttermilk pancakeOne giant pancake with maple syrup, banana and crumbled baconHow to make it300g self-raising flour2 tbsp caster sugar2 eggs400ml buttermilk80g butter100ml maple syrup2 bananas, sliced3 rashers of bacon, cooked crisp and crumbledWhisk the flour, sugar and a pinch of salt. Whisk in the eggs, buttermilk and some melted butter until just combined.Heat a large 28cm non-stick pan over low heat and grease with butter. Pour in all the batter and cover with a lid.Cook until bubbles set on top.Slide onto a plate, flip back in and cook the other side.Top with butter, maple syrup, banana and crumbled bacon.DrinksBuck's chocolate malted milkMilk, chocolate malt, cocoa and vanilla ice cream blended thickHow to make it1 L cold full cream milk6 tbsp chocolate malt powder, plus extra to sprinkle2 tbsp cocoa powder2 tbsp honey4 scoops of vanilla ice creamPut the milk, malt powder, cocoa, honey and ice cream in a blender.Blend until smooth and very frothy.Pour into big glasses, sprinkle malt powder over the froth and serve with straws.Fresh-squeezed orange juicePoured before Buck has his little talk with Bug.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
